result:
Here's what I have so far. Tell me what's wrong or missing.

**What it's for.** You want one place to log your contacts. It replaces the monthly job of retyping the paper notebook into a spreadsheet. You are the main reader. You use it to check whether you have worked a station before. Once a year, you send the whole log to Logbook of The World (LoTW) to confirm contacts for awards. So it must export ADIF, the standard file format for exchanging ham radio logs.

**Where it runs.** You log about 30 contacts a week. You log at home and at field days. Sometimes there is no internet, so it must work fully offline. Lookups must also work offline.

**What I'm filling in (my proposals, not yours):**

- **"Worked before" means the same call sign.** I'd also show the band and mode of each earlier contact, so you can see a new band or mode at a glance. That matters for most awards.
- **Your old spreadsheet comes along.** Lookups would be weak without your history, so I'd import it once.
- **LoTW upload stays your job.** LoTW only accepts logs that its own program, TQSL, signs with your certificate. The tool would write the ADIF file. You'd sign and upload it in TQSL as you do now. Automating that step is possible later, but it's more work.

One thing will shape the build more than anything else. Typing each contact in live at the radio needs fast, keyboard-only entry on whatever device you bring to the field. Typing from the notebook afterward needs a comfortable batch-entry screen at home.

When you're at the radio, at home or in the field, would you type each contact straight into this instead of writing it in the notebook?
